claim_for_writing: Hidden-state alignment can amplify concentration beyond the raw LoRA parameter spectrum.
key_evidence: Functional top-1 exceeds raw top-1 in 8/8 checkpoints by 3.5--27.2 pp using fixed pretrained-base trajectories.
boundary_or_disallowed_claim: Do not call this a necessary causal condition or claim it holds on every free-running LoRA trajectory.

claim_for_writing: All-module HNS strongly reduces extreme LoRA modification on the controlled activation distribution.
key_evidence: Per-layer p99 HNS/LoRA ratio is 0.175--0.581 in 8/8 checkpoints.
boundary_or_disallowed_claim: Do not infer downstream benefit from modification suppression alone.

claim_for_writing: Dominant-head suppression is an important candidate mechanism in math, but it is not universally sufficient.
key_evidence: Both MetaMath checkpoints have HeadOnly greater than TailOnly and ScalarShrink; Qwen MetaMath HeadFro remains Holm-positive.
boundary_or_disallowed_claim: Do not claim HeadOnly generally dominates scalar or that dominant modes are generally excessive.

claim_for_writing: Task utility and functional use intensity are distinct quantities.
key_evidence: Commonsense loses or stays flat despite suppression; localization signs depend on task and scope; SFT-NLL utility can oppose downstream utility.
boundary_or_disallowed_claim: Do not use functional concentration as a signed utility score.

claim_for_writing: Spectral shape may add value beyond matched per-module scale in Qwen MetaMath.
key_evidence: Common-basis HNS minus PerModule is +1.37 pp strict, CI [-0.78,+3.52], and +1.95 pp numeric, CI [0,+4.10].
boundary_or_disallowed_claim: Do not present shape-specific benefit as established; failure to reject zero is not equivalence.

claim_for_writing: HNS offers practical benefit over a calibrated global LoRA scalar.
key_evidence: Common-basis HNS minus calibrated scalar is +0.39 pp strict, CI [-1.56,+2.34], and -0.20 pp numeric, CI [-1.76,+1.56].
boundary_or_disallowed_claim: Do not claim superiority or equivalence; the scalar grid selected its lower boundary gamma=0.4.

claim_for_writing: Low-rank factor representation and run repeatability require separate controls.
key_evidence: Identical adapters are 32/32 token-repeatable across three deterministic processes, while intended-equivalent factor representations change strict status on 3--5/32 enriched questions.
boundary_or_disallowed_claim: Do not interpret the enriched-set rates as population incidence or saved-matrix error as a runtime functional bound.

claim_for_writing: A generic predictor can identify excessive versus task-essential spectral directions.
key_evidence: Raw/functional checkpoint correlations are fragile; FunctionalTop-K does not reliably beat controls; PIQA signed gate and MetaMath reward-gradient pilots stop without usable signal.
boundary_or_disallowed_claim: Do not generalize the tested predictors' failure into impossibility of reward-aligned sensitivity methods.

claim_for_writing: Module-set effects are non-additive and surrogate-dependent.
key_evidence: Observed set utility differs from sums of single-module utility; Qwen Commonsense SFT NLL improves while downstream falls, with the reverse pattern in Magicoder/Llama Tulu.
boundary_or_disallowed_claim: Do not sum single-module utilities into a downstream editing policy.

claim_for_writing: Task family is a stronger qualitative moderator than raw concentration alone in the tested 2x4 grid.
key_evidence: Both bases show positive HNS point estimates on code/math/IF and negative-or-zero on commonsense; MetaMath is the most consistent positive regime.
boundary_or_disallowed_claim: Do not claim universal task-family effects from two bases or treat all Tulu positives as statistically resolved.
